statedReasoning: Bill 181/0, led by Matěj Ondřej Havel and eight co-sponsors including Jiří Pospíšil, Helena Langšádlová, Marek Ženíšek, Michal Kučera and Jan Jakob, amends zákon č. 491/2001 Sb. o volbách do zastupitelstev obcí. Per the full text and důvodová zpráva (read directly from the primary cached text), this is a SINGLE, NARROW change: it lowers the ACTIVE voting-age threshold in municipal-council elections from 18 to 16 (§4/§5), while the PASSIVE right (eligibility to stand as candidate) stays at 18, and all other voter conditions (permanent residence in the municipality, etc.) are unchanged. The DZ's stated rationale is entirely about youth civic-participation theory: forming voting habits early, comparative examples (Austria's full 16+ franchise, German Länder's local/regional 16+ practice, Malta), Austrian turnout/informedness studies for 16-17 year-olds, and a 'no taxation without representation' argument since 16-year-olds already participate economically. The bill explicitly states in its own impact assessment (§9, corruption risks; §12, territorial impacts; §2, EU-law compliance) that it has NO institutional, financial, territorial, or digital-administration component: 'Navrhovaná právní úprava nemá územní dopady... Nedochází ke změně postavení obcí ani k zásahu do jejich pravomocí' and it does not touch election ADMINISTRATION, IT systems, or candidate-list/digital-voting mechanics at all — only the age-eligibility rule.
researchedContext: History confirms: submitted 4 May 2026, distributed 6 May 2026 as print 181/0; government submitted a DISAPPROVING position 3 Jun 2026 (print 181/1, via eKLEP) — the DZ itself gives no reason for opposition since it predates the government's reply, so that specific objection remains unverified from primary text; Organizational Committee recommended proceeding the same day, naming the Constitutional-Legal Committee as guarantor and Kateřina Demetrashvili as rapporteur; no vote as of 24 Jul 2026. Census cross-check: zero undercount — the single recorded amends-edge (491/2001) matches the real full-text scope exactly, confirmed directly (the bill's Čl. I contains only two short amendments to §4 and §5 of that one act).

unstatedEffects.effect: OPEN QUESTION NOW SETTLED: sponsor Jan Jakob holds a supervisory-board seat at Operátor ICT, a.s. (Prague's IT/digital-services SOE). Having now read the full bill text, there is NO election-digitalization, IT-systems, or digital-voter-register content anywhere in the bill — it consists solely of a two-line age-threshold change. Operátor ICT, a.s. has no plausible channel into this specific bill's subject matter; this flag is retracted as a non-finding.

conflictAssessment: The nine sponsors' tied companies are overwhelmingly cultural/civic foundations and municipal/state-owned-enterprise board seats unrelated to election administration: Pospíšil sits on multiple non-profit cultural/regional-development bodies (Nadace Charty 77, Museum Kampa, Muzeum paměti XX. století, Regionální rozvojová agentura Plzeňského kraje, Nadace Věry a Vladimíra Janouškových); Langšádlová sits on Fórum Karla Schwarzenberga, o.p.s.; Ženíšek holds seats at Pojišťovna VZP, a.s. (state-linked health insurer), Pražská energetika, a.s. (Prague-majority-owned energy utility), Plzeňské městské dopravní podniky, a.s. (Pilsen municipal transport), Plzeňská teplárenská, a.s. (Pilsen municipal heating), Národní Centrum Tkání a Buněk a.s. and Kongresové centrum Praha, a.s. (Prague-owned venue); Kučera is jednatel of two small private firms (Sirius Praha s.r.o., LIHT s.r.o.); Jakob sits on Operátor ICT, a.s. (Prague IT SOE). Having now read the actual bill text — a pure age-threshold change (18→16 for active voting only) with explicit no-territorial/no-institutional/no-digital-impact self-assessment — NONE of these ties has any plausible channel into the bill's subject matter, including Jakob's IT-SOE seat, which was the one open question flagged in the first pass and is now cleared. No conflict found; this is one of the cleanest honest-absence cases in the batch given how narrow the bill's actual content is.
